blocks.md: This lesson follows **Prefix Caching Across Turns** in *KV Cache Management* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, KV Cache Management, § Prefix Caching Across Turns
blocks.md: In the connection-pool repair scenario, the agent invocation that processes an integration-test result often begins with the identical system prompt, tool definitions, and historical observations present in the preceding turn. If the serving engine retained the corresponding key-value (KV) activations from that earlier call, it can attach those existing tensors directly to the new request, prefilling only the newly arrived tokens.

questions.q: The section **Prefix Caching Across Turns** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: By Little's law a fixed pool of slots sustains a turn rate inversely proportional to residence, so holding state through a synchronous tool wait divides the memory-bound turn rate by 1 + T_tool/T_model.
During a tool wait the engine keeps, moves, or drops only uniquely reclaimable blocks, and offloading pays only when the wait exceeds the transfer round trip and memory is contested.

A content-keyed radix tree finds the longest retained common prefix, leaf-first eviction keeps residency prefix-closed, and efficacy is the token-weighted hit rate after availability, permission, and block rounding.
A reusable prefix must be compatible, available, and permitted, and none of the three says whether the evidence is current, so freshness is enforced by the harness rewriting the prompt.
